objective: Publish an approved packet on four social channels
evidenceSource: Independent observer snapshot; private source identifiers retained in .omb-scratch/liz-handoff-20261022/report.json
observed: The user requested publication, then reported the X connection and browser recovery were not working.
The agent checked X, Bluesky and Threads sign-in state. This was discovery, not publication.
The X connector reported zero active connections. A browser sign-in request was issued for X.
Browser restart was refused while the person controlled the browser. The agent was instructed to wait for control to be returned.
The agent checked other computer availability, attached assets and instructed the user to publish all four posts manually and return their URLs.
The final recovery request has one runtime node and no delegated escalation. Its conversational execution completed.
No Mastodon site visit or publication receipt is present in the inspected publication attempt.

assessment.qualification: Bluesky and Threads were inspected. It would be inaccurate to say neither was tried at all. The record does not establish that posting on either was possible at that moment.
assessment.authorityBoundary: Human browser takeover and declined authentication must be respected. Recovery must not bypass either.

rootCauseHypothesis.claim: Darcy delegated a four-channel publishing task beyond Liz's established skills.

expectedBehaviour: Darcy retains the overall publishing objective and delegates four separate channel-specific tasks while Liz develops the corresponding skills. Compose them into one task only once all four skills are enabled and demonstrated in execution.
Keep ownership of publication while seeking help with the specific connector/browser blocker.
Track each channel separately: discovery attempted, access verified or unknown, publication attempted, receipt verified, waiting or blocked.
Apply a shared blocker only to routes that actually depend on it; preserve independent work and untested routes explicitly.
Escalate a failed recovery with tool evidence and the smallest required assistance; retain the approved packet and resume point.
Request only an unavoidable human action such as authentication or handing browser control back, without transferring publication itself.
Verify each post from its actual receipt; partial completion cannot satisfy the four-channel objective.
nextEvaluation: Observe each channel-specific task separately: verified publication, retained ownership, scoped blockers and escalation. Compare subsequent executions with this combined-task failure. Record which skill version was available and used; a skill file or a completed turn alone does not establish readiness for the combined workflow.

observed: Darcy dispatched an X-only assignment that also requested creating all four Todoist subtasks and creating/enabling a channel skill.
The referenced X brief was absent at the first read; a later read found all four briefs.
Liz reached a working X login form; no authenticated account was established in the inspected evidence.
Liz then performed four-channel task administration and skill discovery while the X authentication dependency remained unresolved.
followUp.lesson: Separating channel names is insufficient if the executor still receives unrelated coordination work and premature skill construction. Handoff prerequisites must exist before dispatch. A learned skill should be derived from observed execution; an untested draft must remain labelled as such.
followUp.scope: This review records evidence and a proposed correction. It does not establish the final result of the running assignment or change bot configuration.
